title: Scoped Pause Safety (Bounded Halt with Preserved Exit, Parameterized over Scope)

dascp.note: Account-scope instance: BPO:0051 STRENGTHENS C30-S by requiring the per-account pause to either auto-expire or always permit a forced-recovery path; C30-S's white-paper text mandates the pause capability but not its boundedness.
Token-scope instance: BPO:0051 STRENGTHENS C31-S in the same way at per-token scope; the freeze-forever-by-scope failure mode is excluded by construction here but not by C31-S as written.

descriptions.semantic: Given a well-defined scope σ — system, per-account, per-token, or any combination drawn from the access-control configuration — when σ is in the paused mode, every value-moving transition whose effect intersects σ is disabled (safety); the pause of σ can be entered only by a principal authorized for σ and lifted only by an authorized path; and the pause cannot deprive entitled parties within σ of their funds indefinitely: it either auto-expires after a bounded delay or always leaves a forced-recovery edge open for entitled withdrawals at σ.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A mode-switched LTS whose mode space is the product of per-scope on/off flags; the pause flag of σ restricts the σ-touching transition relation to non-value-moving (and recovery) transitions, plus a meta-constraint that σ's paused mode is not absorbing for entitled exits at σ (bounded sojourn or always-available exit edge whose enabling is mode-independent at σ).
descriptions.security: Scoped pause is the granular form of the circuit-breaker control: it lets a system contain an active exploit, a compliance event, or a custody dispute to a single account or token without freezing every honest user. The unbounded-pause-by-scope failure mode is real — a per-account pause without an exit is the same seizure-by-freeze as a system-wide one, just narrower. This property excludes that failure by construction.
descriptions.execution_semantics: A `whenScopeNotPaused(σ)` modifier gates value-moving functions whose effect-set intersects σ. Pause and unpause are σ-authorized actions. The bounded clause adds either a timelocked auto-unpause at σ (block.timestamp ≥ pausedAt(σ) + maxPause(σ) ⇒ effectively unpaused for σ) or an always-callable forced-exit-at-σ that ignores the pause flag for entitled withdrawals at σ. Violations: scope-pause without an exit, coverage gaps (a value-moving path inside σ that lacks the σ-guard), unprivileged scope-pause, or a scope-pause that suspends the very recovery edge intended to escape it.
descriptions.formal_verification: Two obligations per scope σ. (1) SAFETY — under paused(σ), no value-moving σ-touching transition is enabled (model-check / SMT over the σ-gated transition set, plus coverage that every value-moving selector whose effects intersect σ is σ-gated). (2) BOUNDED LIVENESS — paused(σ) is not absorbing for entitled exits at σ; requires the same fairness machinery as BPO:0002 (or a structural escape edge whose enabling is σ-mode-independent, making it SMT-checkable). The system-scope specialization is BPO:0050; per-account and per-token specializations specialize to σ = {account} and σ = {token}.

formalization.signature: Scope σ drawn from the access-control configuration (system, account, token, asset-class); mode(σ, s) ∈ {active, paused}; pausedAt(σ, s) : timestamp; maxPause(σ) : const ; valueMoving ⊆ Op; effects(o) : Op → 2^Scope ; recovery(σ) ⊆ Op.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Scope pause safety:  ∀ s, s', o, σ . ( mode(σ, s) = paused ∧ o ∈ valueMoving ∧ σ ∈ effects(o) ∧ o ∉ recovery(σ) ∧ s --[o]--> s' ) → False.
Coverage:  ∀ σ, o ∈ valueMoving . σ ∈ effects(o) → gatedBy(o, whenScopeNotPaused(σ)).
Bounded sojourn at σ:  ∀ s, σ . mode(σ, s) = paused → ◇_{≤ maxPause(σ)} ( mode(σ, ·) = active ∨ exitAvailable(σ) ).
Exit preservation at σ:  ∀ s, σ, p . entitledWithdrawal(p, σ, s) → enabled(forcedExit(p, σ), s) (σ-mode-independent).

temporal_logic.ltl: G( ∀σ . paused(σ) → ¬anyValueMoveTouching(σ) )   ∧   G( ∀σ . paused(σ) → F_{bounded(σ)} ( active(σ) ∨ exitTaken(σ) ) )
temporal_logic.ctl: AG( ∀σ . paused(σ) → AF active(σ) )   under the timelock or always-on-escape assumption
temporal_logic.fairness: REQUIRED for the timelock variant: weak fairness on block-clock progress (BPO:0080). NOT required for the structural-escape variant (the recovery edge is unconditionally enabled in σ's paused mode).

hoare.pre: mode(σ) = paused ∧ o ∈ valueMoving ∧ σ ∈ effects(o) ∧ o ∉ recovery(σ)

hoare.post: funds returned to p regardless of mode(σ)

formalization.state_machine: Per-scope two-mode automaton; pause(σ) / unpause(σ) are σ-admin-gated edges; auto-unpause(σ) fires when the σ-clock guard holds; a forced-exit(σ) edge is enabled in both modes for entitled holders at σ. The property is the conjunction, over every scope σ in scope of the policy, of (no value-move edge whose effect-set intersects σ is enabled from σ-paused) and (σ-paused is not absorbing for entitled exits at σ).
formalization.type_theoretic: The pause capability at σ is a bounded, possibly time-limited, scope-typed capability (an affine resource with a scope tag and an expiry), distinct from an unbounded admin capability. Specializes naturally to σ = system (BPO:0050), σ = account (C30-S instance), σ = token (C31-S instance).

relationships.note: System-scope sibling: BPO:0050 is the σ = system specialization; BPO:0051 carries the same safety/liveness structure parameterized over arbitrary scopes.
An UNBOUNDED scope-pause negates eventual-withdrawal for parties within σ — the same tension BPO:0050 hosts at system scope. This bounded form is the designed resolution at scope σ.
An L2-style structural escape can realize the exit-preservation clause at the relevant σ.
Pause/unpause authority at σ is governed by access-control correctness.

attack_surface.pattern: per-account or per-token pause with neither time bound nor exit; equivalent to scoped seizure of funds
attack_surface.notes: The whole reason this property is specified as bounded at every σ.

attack_surface.pattern: a value-moving path whose effect intersects σ is not σ-gated; pause is ineffective and the exploit continues against σ
attack_surface.notes: Coverage obligation: enumerate, per σ, every value-moving selector whose effects intersect σ and gate each.

attack_surface.pattern: a single per-scope guardian key freezes σ maliciously
attack_surface.notes: Multisig / timelock the scope-pause authority; keep unpause less privileged or auto-timed.

attack_surface.pattern: the forced-exit edge for σ is itself disabled by the σ-pause, defeating the exit clause
attack_surface.notes: The recovery edge must be σ-mode-INDEPENDENT by construction.

metrics: pause duration per σ vs maxPause(σ)
fraction of value-moving selectors gated per σ
invariant_checkpoints: all value-moving selectors whose effects intersect σ carry whenScopeNotPaused(σ)
forcedExit(p, σ) reachable in σ-paused mode for entitled p

strategies.notes: Prove, for each σ the system supports, that every value-moving method whose effect-set intersects σ is σ-gated and reverts when σ is paused.
Check that σ-paused is not absorbing for entitled exits at σ under the clock/escape assumption, for each scope in the policy.

testability: all σ-intersecting value-moving calls revert when σ is paused
forcedExit(σ) succeeds while σ is paused

runtime: whenScopeNotPaused(σ) on every value-moving path whose effect-set intersects σ
always-enabled forcedExit(σ) for entitled withdrawals at σ
static: coverage check: no σ-intersecting value-moving selector is σ-ungated
design_patterns: separate (lower) authority for σ-unpause vs σ-pause

assumptions.statement: Block clock advances so per-scope auto-unpause guards can fire (only for the timelock variant).
Per-scope pause authority is not unilaterally controlled by a single untrusted key.
The effect-set effects(o) of every value-moving operation is precisely modelled, so per-scope coverage is decidable.

sources: circuit-breaker patterns at per-account and per-token granularity
provenance.notes: Authored as the scope-parameterized companion to BPO:0050. The DASCP C30-S (account) and C31-S (token) controls are addressed by instantiating σ = account and σ = token respectively; the per-link notes flag the same strengthening pattern BPO:0050 records for C29-S (bounded + exit go beyond the bare DASCP capability text).
